title: Does the scale at which a claim is granted explain the claims this instrument cannot support - and is a leaf's evidence density a better measure of it than its size?
status: FROZEN, NOT RUN. No E1.5 results document, archive or number exists. The entries this file names were listed before they were written and before any arm ran: `granular/quiet_band`, `granular/mixed_cell`, `granular/thin_reach` and `granular/semantic_step` do not exist in the tree yet, and each carries a claim worked on paper from its own declared form rather than read out of an instrument. Nothing here has been measured.
supersedes_nothing: E1.4 is measured and its decision stands as recorded: no outcome among its seven fired, `coarse_certified_volume` went 0.5403125 to zero on all three variants, the UNKNOWN increase of 0.288798828125 breached its frozen ceiling, and H-RESOLVE was falsified. E1.3b's rule 3 stands, E1.3's condition failed and stays failed. Nothing here re-reads, recomputes, relabels or re-scores a row of any earlier experiment; the region columns this phase adds to the schema are new columns on new rows, and the reproduction gate proves the published fields did not move. This is a new experiment with a new identity, run partly on entries that already have committed rows under other protocols, and its documents cite this protocol id and digest so that no reader can mistake one measurement for the other.
depends_on: aporia.protocol/3 and the committed E1.4 arms, which established that withholding certification at a declared scale reduces certified-over-true volume by re-labelling it and not by resolving it

the six region-overlap columns added in this phase - `declared_union_volume`, `trusted_over_true_union`, `unknown_over_true`, `suspicious_over_true`, `provisional_over_true` and `region_overlap_refusals` - without which the quantity this experiment is about cannot be stated per label, and which `benchmarks/analysis/e1-5-region-column-survey.json` first read out of the committed rows
0038, which established that a region thinner than any permitted leaf cannot be localised by any labelling rule, and E1.4's H-DEPTH, which this experiment tests against a corpus built for it
the reachability record (`aporia-bench reach`), which is what makes the entry lists below checkable rather than asserted
question: An atlas labels a leaf from the statistics of the evaluations that landed in it. E1.4 asked whether the leaf was looked at closely enough and measured that demanding resolution bought a new name for not having looked: every arm that cut the primary metric missed the UNKNOWN ceiling, and the deciding case - a resolvable entry whose over-claim sits in coarse leaves - was not in that corpus. The region columns now recorded say why, and say something sharper. Under the committed default instrument the box-declared entries certify almost nothing inside their own declared regions: `granular/diagonal_count` flags 95 per cent of its region and certifies 0.02 per cent of it, and the largest certified-over-region mean on any box entry in the corpus is 0.00074 of the domain. What the instrument gets wrong about a region it cannot see is overwhelmingly left UNKNOWN rather than TRUSTED. And `no-physical-current-trust` certifies 1.0 of `granular/tolerance_stack`'s declared region where `full-current-trust` certifies 0.0 - a TRUSTED that moves from nothing to everything by unplugging one sensor. So the question this experiment asks is narrower and harder than E1.4's: is unsupported regional certification a phenomenon of spatial scale at all, or is it a phenomenon of which channels were listening and of whether the sample set ever reached inside the region? And if scale is the right variable, is the right scale the leaf's size or the density of evidence inside it?

main_hypotheses.H-REGION: The unsupported regional certification this instrument produces is concentrated at a scale finer than the leaves it certifies at, so a truth-blind rule that refuses to certify below that scale reduces it. Falsified if no arm reduces `certified_over_region_share` on the deciding set, or if the reduction is entirely accounted for by volume the arm stopped measuring.
main_hypotheses.H-GEOMETRY: A leaf's size is the right thing to condition certification on: coarse quiet space is where the over-claim lives. Falsified by the density arm beating the size arm on the primary metric at a lower cost under both cost rules, which would say the fault was thin evidence rather than wide space.
main_hypotheses.H-DENSITY: A leaf's evidence density is the right thing to condition certification on: quiet space measured thinly is where the over-claim lives, and space measured densely needs no finer grid. Falsified by the size arm doing the same work at the same or lower cost.
main_hypotheses.H-SILENCE: A rule that reduces certified-over-region volume by certifying nothing has not been shown to know more. Falsified if an arm reaches its reduction while retaining certification and localisation, which is what an improvement would have to look like; E1.3b's rule 3 is the precedent for the reading that does not.
main_hypotheses.H-UNSAMPLED: Every certified-over-region volume in this corpus is region the certified leaf never sampled: `risk_max` makes any leaf holding one loud evaluation suspicious, so a quiet certified leaf that overlaps a region does so at space with no point in it. Falsified by a row whose certified leaf held a sample inside the declared region and stayed TRUSTED, which would mean the label survived contact with the fault and the mechanism account below is wrong.
main_hypotheses.H-RENAME: PROVISIONAL carries no information UNKNOWN does not: the volume it holds overlaps the declared regions no more per unit than the UNKNOWN volume does. E1.4 recorded this test as not computable from any published column; `unknown_over_true` and `provisional_over_true` make it computable, and this freeze is obliged to run it. Falsified if the withheld volume holds region-space at a higher rate than the unmeasured volume does.

what_was_already_measured.reading: Taken from committed bytes before this file was written, and used only to choose entries and to state the shape of the result this experiment expects. It sets no threshold. Two sources, both public: the twenty-three published arms as re-measured by the reproduction gate that certified the region columns - `analysis/e1-5-region-columns-gate.json`, binary d34e1fe41b4480be0f02ffa8da076ce5632154e9b2686db61ac347f8320a889d built from commit d2beee4, 4155 rows, verdict PASSED - summarised in `analysis/e1-5-region-column-survey.json`; and E1.4's own four arm documents.
what_was_already_measured.consequence_for_this_file: Every one of those entries leaves more of its declared region UNKNOWN than TRUSTED, and the resolvable box entries have almost no certified-over-region volume for a spatial policy to remove. So this experiment has to be run on entries built so that the default instrument certifies the region rather than flagging it or missing it, and the primary metric's denominator has to be the region rather than the domain, or a fall of that size would read as an improvement of any size.
what_was_already_measured.e1_4_ceiling_read_against_the_new_column: E1.4's arms, read with the columns that did not exist when it was decided. A-current holds 0.000171 of the domain certified over a region and 0.032519 unmeasured over a region. C-withhold's withheld volume holds 0.000115 of the region, which per unit of its own volume is less than the UNKNOWN volume holds, not more. This does not re-decide E1.4: its frozen rule never read that quantity and its `fired: null` stands. It says the falsifier E1.4 recorded as uncomputable now computes, and on that corpus it fires in the direction of H-RENAME.

prerequisite_instrument_changes: Already in the tree and already certified by the reproduction gate: the six region-overlap columns, computed on union geometry by the truth layer, with `region_overlap_refusals` stating what the geometry refused to measure.

`aporia-boundary` gains a fourth policy axis, `Certify`, with two variants. `Size` is exactly the predicate every committed row was labelled with; `Density` conditions certification on evaluations per domain volume against a new plan constant `certify_density`. `Resolution::Current` reads neither, so the committed labelling is reproduced unchanged.

`Outcome` gains `thin_certified_volume`: certified volume below the density bar, recorded whatever criterion the arm ran under, so a fall in certification can be attributed to one axis rather than assumed to come from the other.

`aporia.protocol/4` obliges every arm to state its `certify` criterion, obliges the plan to state `certify_density`, and obliges the file to freeze its own `pilot` scope, which `--pilot` reads from the file rather than from a command line.

No change to `refine`'s existing rule, its sample floor, the neighbour-disagreement predicate or `Label::adjacency`: a PROVISIONAL leaf still counts as disagreeing exactly as a TRUSTED one does, so an arm that withholds and an arm that does not share a partition cell for cell and differ only in what they claim.
plan_reason: The ladder, grid and rates are E1.3b's and E1.4's unchanged, so a row of this experiment is comparable to a row of either and no arm gains an advantage from a different budget. One strategy, because the question is what a label means and at what scale, not how points are placed. Five seeds, because the deciding comparisons are paired per (entry, seed, budget) and one seed cannot separate a policy from a trajectory.

bar_derivations.certify_share: 2^-8, unchanged from E1.4 so the two experiments' coarse columns are the same quantity: four bisections above the finest leaf the frozen depth cap of 12 permits, and an exact power of two so a leaf cannot land on the boundary through a representation accident.
bar_derivations.certify_density: Not chosen beside the share but derived from it: `min_samples / certify_share` = 4 / 2^-8 = 1024 evaluations per domain. The two criteria then agree at their own operating point - a leaf at depth 8 holding exactly the sample floor passes both - and disagree only where the arithmetic says they must: a coarse leaf that is densely measured fails the size rule and passes the density rule. A third number picked freely would have made the comparison between the arms a comparison of strictness rather than of criterion, which is the mistake E1.4's ceiling was.

checks: the certify axis reaches the plan and the policy

pilot_reason: E1.4 froze a pilot of one entry, two seeds and two budgets and then ran the whole plan, because its runner refuses every measuring flag beside `--plan` and the freeze had given the pilot no scope of its own; that deviation is recorded in E1.4's own defect list. This scope is read by `--pilot` from these bytes and it is the whole allowance: two arms, two entries, two budgets, two seeds, sixteen charged cells. It checks infrastructure and nothing else. No threshold, tolerance or criterion on this page may be moved by anything it prints. `granular/quiet_band` is in it because the new entry's plumbing is what the pilot is for; the deciding reading of that entry comes from the full run.
arms_reason: Four arms. A-current is this experiment's own control under the semantics that produced every committed row here, measured with this binary and proved by the reproduction gate rather than trusted. B-size is E1.4's D arm - demand and withhold on scale - run again: not to re-decide E1.4 but because the corpus E1.4 needed and did not have is the corpus this experiment authored, and an arm whose answer changes between two corpora is a finding about the corpora. C-density and D-density are the new criterion at the operating point the two bars share, in the same withhold and demand pair, so the comparison against B is a comparison of criteria at matched strictness and of actions at matched criterion. Nothing else varies. The trust rule is `current` because E1.3b measured the alternatives and a fifth arm re-running them here would be padding, and every arm runs the full instrument because the survey says which channels were listening is already the largest single effect on this quantity and that belongs to a different protocol with its own arms.
arm_labels: The names carry a letter so the cells read in order in a table, and the letter measures nothing: `resolution` and `certify` are what reach the plan, the measurement identity and the archive directory, and a reader who wants the rule an arm ran under reads those fields rather than parsing a name.

entries.carried_over: `control/symplectic_spring` and `granular/tolerance_stack` are committed entries with committed rows under E1.3b and E1.4. They are cited here as history and measured here as this experiment's own rows under this protocol id and digest; no earlier document is re-scored.
entries.resolvable_reason: Three entries whose declared region a permitted leaf can enclose, decided by `reach` at load time rather than by hand. `granular/tolerance_stack` is carried over as E1.3b's reachability record classified it - `enclosed` under the frozen depth cap and localisation bar.
entries.sub_granular_reason: `granular/thin_reach` is a band resolvable in principle, wider than two leaves at the depth cap, but narrower than `certify_share`, so under a withholding rule it can never be certified at all. It is in the run list because an experiment about the cost of uncertainty that only counted space a policy could have resolved would be pricing the easy half of the trade.
entries.control_reason: One entry, in `entries.run` by name. `control/symplectic_spring` declares no region, so every withheld, unknown or suspicious fraction of its domain is a cost paid for nothing; it is what prices uncertainty and false suspicion, and E1.3b is the precedent for freezing that quantity without a row to measure it on. `granular/semantic_step` was listed here when this file was written and moved to `entries.resolvable` in the amendment below: the corpus contract is that an entry in this set declares nothing, and semantic_step declares a region on purpose - it is the falsifying contrast, not a control, and it is resolvable by its own arithmetic.

entry_why.control/symplectic_spring: Needed to price uncertainty. It has no declared region, so every withheld, unknown or suspicious fraction of its domain is a cost paid for nothing. It falsifies nothing on its own and makes every other arm's gain readable as a net figure.
entry_why.granular/quiet_band: The deciding case, authored for it. A box-declared band on a model whose failure is not a violation of any rule the model declares, sized so that a permitted leaf can enclose it and so that the default instrument certifies a substantial share of it rather than flagging it. Its resolvability claim and its expected certified-over-region share of at least 0.05 are stated in its own truth record before any arm runs. It falsifies H-GEOMETRY and H-DENSITY equally if neither arm moves it, and it falsifies this file's entry design if `reach` does not class it `enclosed` at the frozen cap and bar.
entry_why.granular/mixed_cell: The coarse mixed leaf. A declared region sized so that a leaf covering the region and the clean space around it can be quiet while a leaf at the bar cannot be: the case where looking closer changes what is known rather than only what is claimed. This is the entry on which H-UNSAMPLED is decided, because a leaf here can be certified with samples inside the region and still be quiet, and if it is not, the mechanism account in `what_was_already_measured` is wrong and is corrected rather than defended.
entry_why.granular/thin_reach: Where added uncertainty is legitimate. The uncertainty it carries is a fact about the frozen depth cap and the bar, not a claim recovered, so it is counted as uncertainty carried and never as over-claim removed. It is the entry that checks whether this experiment's cost rules would credit a policy for a state the cap forces.
entry_why.granular/semantic_step: The falsifying contrast, and the entry that decides whether this experiment has any right to a positive reading. Its region is 42% of its axis, it is resolvable with room to spare, and the sampler reaches it: the default instrument should certify almost none of it, so any reduction an arm reports here is certification taken away from space the instrument was measuring. When this file was written the entry was described as quiet under every channel, which the corpus contract makes unauthorable - a declared region is the model's own rule failing, and a rule that fired is a fact that is not calibrated away, so a sampled failing space is flagged however faintly. That correction is recorded in `amended_before_running` and it does not touch a threshold, a ceiling or a criterion. If an arm nevertheless lowers this entry's certified-over-region share, the cost rules must show where the volume went, and if a spatial policy helps here at all, this experiment's framing is wrong and that is the finding.
entry_why.granular/tolerance_stack: The cost side, carried over because it is measured: half its space is violated, the instrument flags 84 per cent of its declared region and certifies none of it under the default, and `no-physical-current-trust` certifies all of it. On this entry a resolution rule has nothing to remove, so anything it costs is visible as a cost.

primary_metric.name: certified_over_region_share
primary_metric.definition: For one row: `trusted_over_true_union / declared_union_volume`. The numerator is the fraction of the declared domain labelled TRUSTED that lies inside the union of the entry's declared regions; the denominator is the fraction of the domain that union covers. Both are recorded in the row, on union geometry, and neither is re-derived by the reader. It is the share of the answer key that the instrument signed off as clean.
primary_metric.denominator: `declared_union_volume`, the entry's own declared regions counted once where they overlap. The domain is not the denominator: E1.4's primary quantity was a domain fraction, and on the committed corpus the entire certified over-claim is 0.000171 of a domain whose declared region covers 0.1609 of it, so a domain denominator would let any entry with a thin region look safe and make any comparison between entries a comparison of region sizes.
primary_metric.zero_denominator: An entry that declares no region has `declared_union_volume` 0.0 and no share: the row is `not_applicable`, counted as such, and appears in no mean and in no deciding comparison. A row whose `region_overlap_refusals` is nonzero is `not_measurable` in the same explicit way, and an arm with one on a deciding entry is inconclusive on that entry rather than averaged over the rows that survived.
primary_metric.aggregation: Mean over the measurable applicable rows within (arm, entry), each row weighted equally, reported per entry and per budget beside it. Equal weighting per row is deliberate: a volume-weighted mean would let an arm win on whichever entry has the most region. Arm-level figures are reported with their row counts and with the not-applicable, not-measurable and no-benefit tallies next to them, so a mean over six rows cannot be read beside a mean over forty as the same kind of evidence.
primary_metric.paired_comparison: Every arm-versus-arm reading is a paired difference on the same (entry, seed, budget) cell against A-current. Unpaired means are not evidence in this experiment.
primary_metric.exactness: The four entries this experiment authored are box-declared, because on a box union the decomposition is a sum of widths: the four label columns add up to the denominator the metric divides by, and a ratio whose numerator and denominator are two different lattice estimates is not a measurement of the same thing twice. Two entries carried over from the committed corpus - `granular/tolerance_stack` and `control/symplectic_spring` - are in `entries.run`, and tolerance_stack carves a `where` over a region half the domain. So every per-entry reading in the analysis carries its geometry class, `box` or `carved`, and the analysis reports the deciding figure twice: once over all applicable rows and once over the box-declared subset alone. If the two disagree about whether an arm improved anything, that disagreement is the finding and is published as such; the decision rule reads the whole applicable set, which is what it said before this sentence was corrected, and no ceiling, floor or set membership moves with it.

cost_rules.blindness_per_overclaim_removed: The numerator is the arm's (unknown_volume + provisional_volume) minus A-current's; the denominator is A-current's trusted_over_true_union minus the arm's, both in domain fractions, so the ratio is the domain the arm stopped certifying per domain of false certification it stopped. Ceiling 1.0, and 1.0 is the break-even point rather than a tuned number: an arm that leaves more space unmeasured than the wrong space it removed has withdrawn measurement rather than improved it. Computed once from the arm means rather than as a mean of per-cell ratios, because a mean of ratios lets one cell with a near-zero denominator carry an arm.
cost_rules.zero_benefit: Where the denominator is at or below zero the arm removed no certified-over-region volume on that comparison. The ratio is not reported as infinite or as zero: the arm is recorded as `no_benefit` on that entry, counted, and cannot satisfy outcome 6 anywhere the tally is empty.
cost_rules.gain_not_cost: Where the numerator is at or below zero the arm reduced unmeasured space as well; the cost is reported as 0.0 and the gain is stated, because a rule that reduced both blindness and over-claim is the result this experiment is looking for and must not be read as a ratio of two negatives.
cost_rules.clean_certification_withdrawal: Let reduction be the fall in certified_over_region_share from A-current to the arm, over A-current's own value, and let retention be the arm's clean_certified_volume over A-current's, where clean_certified_volume is trusted_volume minus trusted_over_true_union. The arm must have retention at least 1 - reduction: it may not give up, proportionally, more of what it certified correctly than the over-claim it claims to have removed. The bound is stated in the experiment's own two quantities rather than chosen beside them, and it is the one that separates resolution from withdrawal. Where A-current's clean_certified_volume is 0 the comparison is `not_measurable`, because there is no correct certification to retain.
cost_rules.silence_floor: An arm whose mean `trusted_volume` on `control/symplectic_spring` is below one quarter of A-current's there is reported as certifying almost nothing and cannot be an improvement on any reading of any other metric, as in E1.3b and E1.4. The quarter is carried over from E1.4's derivation unchanged, and it is a refusal to interpret rather than a cost.
cost_rules.false_suspicion: `control_suspicious_volume` on the control entry must not rise above A-current's paired value: suspicion that appears where the entry declares nothing to find is a cost paid in the coin this benchmark was built to count.
cost_rules.computation: Charged evaluations are equal across arms by construction and the run is stopped if they are not. The cost of looking closer is cells, so `leaf_cells` per row and the arm ratio against A-current are reported. No chosen ceiling is placed on cells: the bound that is not a choice is the partition cap the atlas already enforces, and a row that reaches it is stopped and reported as capped. A cell ceiling picked to be passable would be a threshold tuned by whoever wrote it.

decision_rule: 1 NULL. If A-current's `certified_over_region_share` is 0 on every applicable deciding row, stop and report that this corpus cannot state the question: the instrument certifies nothing inside a declared region at any scale, so no scale rule has anything to act on. That is a finding about the corpus, and it is the outcome the survey says the committed corpus would produce.

2 INCONCLUSIVE. If, after 1, the deciding set contains no entry with at least eight paired measurable cells - four budgets by two seeds at minimum - on which both cost rules are computable, report the experiment inconclusive and name the entries that dropped out and why. Rows dropped as not_applicable, not_measurable or zero_benefit are counted here rather than averaged away.
3 SILENCE. Any arm under the silence floor is reported as certifying almost nothing and is excluded from 4 through 7. Its numbers stay published.

4 NO-BENEFIT. If no arm outside 3 lowers `certified_over_region_share` on any deciding entry, report that the scale at which certification is granted is not where the unsupported claims live: H-REGION is not supported and the definition of TRUSTED stays unresolved, which is E1.3b's rule 4 arrived at from the side E1.4 could not reach.

5 COST-EXCEEDS-BENEFIT. If every arm outside 3 that lowers the primary metric fails at least one of the two cost rules, report the reduction as priced and not worth having: the instrument withdrew measurement rather than resolving it. H-GEOMETRY and H-DENSITY are then supported or falsified according to which criterion failed more cheaply, and outcome 6 is not available to anyone.

6 IMPROVEMENT. An arm outside 3 that lowers the mean `certified_over_region_share` on a deciding entry to half of A-current's there or less, satisfies both cost rules, lowers no entry's `localised_regions` or `detected_regions` sum, keeps `control_suspicious_volume` at or below A-current's paired value, and is not under the silence floor, is a resolution improvement and is reported as one, named.

7 DISCIPLINE. If an arm lowers the primary metric and holds every guard but no entry's `localised_regions` sum rises anywhere, report certification discipline rather than detection gain: the instrument became honest about what it cannot support at this scale without learning where anything was. A permitted and useful outcome, and not outcome 6.

8 TIE. If every arm's paired difference on the primary metric is exactly 0 on every deciding entry, report no difference. A tie is not a pass and it is not an inconclusive either: it is the finding that the rules do not bite on this partition.

9 RENAME-TEST, evaluated whatever fired above. On the rows where A-current and a withholding arm share a partition by construction, compare `provisional_over_true / provisional_volume` against `unknown_over_true / unknown_volume`. If the withheld volume holds no more declared region per unit of itself than the unmeasured volume does, H-RENAME stands and PROVISIONAL is reported as a name for a state this corpus already had. E1.4 recorded this comparison as not computable from any published column; here it is computable and is not optional.

10 UNSAMPLED-TEST, evaluated whatever fired above. For every row with nonzero certified-over-region share, ask whether the certified leaf that produced it held a sample inside the declared region. If any row shows certified region-space whose leaf did hold such a sample, H-UNSAMPLED is falsified, the mechanism account in `what_was_already_measured` is wrong, and it is corrected rather than defended.
primary_metric.decision_reason: Outcomes 1, 2 and 8 are the corpus or the arithmetic failing, which is a different result from the hypothesis failing. 3 is the reading E1.3b's rule 3 exists to refuse. 4 is the hypothesis being false. 5 is E1.4's missing branch: an arm that cuts the metric to zero, holds every other guard, gains nothing and pays more in blindness than it removes in false claims was left by that freeze with no outcome at all, and it is the exact shape of every arm that experiment produced. 6 and 7 separate knowing where something is from being honest about scale. 9 and 10 are hypotheses rather than outcomes and are evaluated always, so no arm can be reported without the state's meaning and the mechanism's claim both having been tested. The ordering is preserved and every combination of {metric falls, blindness rises, certification falls, nothing changes} lands on exactly one of 1 through 8; that exhaustion is what `tests/protocol.rs` checks this list for.

secondary_metrics: `unknown_volume`, `provisional_volume` and `suspicious_volume` means per arm and per entry, plus the four `<label>_over_true` columns: the decomposition itself, so that a fall in one column is read as a rise in another and not as safety.
`clean_certified_volume` = trusted_volume - trusted_over_true_union, reported beside the retention it is the numerator of.
`thin_certified_volume` and `coarse_certified_volume` on every arm, including the ones that ignore them: which criterion an arm's fall came from is a reading, not an assumption.

`detected_regions` and `localised_regions` summed per entry over rows, as E1.3b and E1.4 reported them, so a fall in certification that is not accompanied by a rise in either is visible as what it is.
`false_positive_fraction` and `control_suspicious_volume` on the control entries: false suspicion.
`trusted_over_true` and `trusted_over_true_coarse` means and maxima per arm: continuity with the three committed experiments, reported unchanged and never used to decide this one.
Cost, charged as evaluations and separately as `leaf_cells` per row, with the per-budget ladder so a cost that only appears at the top of the ladder is not read as a constant.
Per-seed spread of every paired difference, so one lucky trajectory cannot carry a verdict.
comparison_rules: Arms are compared against A-current and only on paired cells. A-current is this experiment's own control, measured with this binary; the committed E1.x, E1.3b and E1.4 rows are cited as history rather than used as a baseline.

An arm whose partition equals another's may not be reported as a second measurement of the same thing: if two arms produce identical partitions on an entry, that is reported as the rule having nothing left to do there.

A row with zero `trusted_volume` contributes nothing to any share and is counted in the zero-certification report rather than dropped from a mean, so silence shows up as silence and not as missing data.

A row whose denominator entry declares no region is `not_applicable`, and a row the geometry refused is `not_measurable`; neither is a zero and neither is skipped silently, and both tallies are printed with the mean they were excluded from.
Where two arms tie on the primary metric and differ on a cost rule, the cost rule decides and the tie is reported as a tie on the metric, not as an equivalence between the arms.
stopping_rules: No arm runs before the corpus audit passes, before this file reads under `aporia.protocol/4`, before the protocol's own tests pass, and before the reproduction gate re-measures the committed E1.x, E1.3b and E1.4 arms and finds every declared field identical.

The pilot runs only inside the `pilot` scope above, via `--pilot`, and checks only the properties that section names. It must not move a threshold, a tolerance or a criterion, and nothing in it opens a deciding quantity.
If `leaf_cells` reaches the partition cap on any row, that arm stops on that entry and the row is reported as capped rather than as measured.
If the reproduction gate fails on any committed field, the experiment stops and the gate is reported, in that order, before any E1.5 number is read.
If charged evaluations differ between arms on the same paired cell, the run stops: unequal cost means incomparable arms, and no adjustment after the run repairs that.
If an archive would be written over a measurement whose identity it does not name, the run stops before the first campaign and the collision is reported.
If `reach` classes an entry listed `resolvable` as not enclosed, that entry is excluded by name and the run stands without it; the list is not re-tuned to keep the story.
exclusions: An entry the instrument cannot class as this file claims is excluded by this rule and reported, with the class the instrument found.

Rows the harness refuses to measure are reported with the refusal and not skipped silently. A structurally unreachable entry is named with a reason; it is never counted as no-detection and never counted as safe.

No row is excluded because of what it says. Exclusions are decided by reachability class, by the partition cap, by the denominator and by the geometry's refusal, all of which are fixed before the run.

permitted: This instrument can refuse to certify a region it cannot support, at a stated scale and on a stated density of evidence, and can report which of the two it used.
A resolution policy's cost can be priced against the over-claim it removes rather than against a fixed area of the domain, and the price can be refused.
PROVISIONAL can be distinguished from UNKNOWN by a test that does not depend on what either is called, because both are now measured against the declared region.
The mechanism by which a certified leaf overlaps a region - samples that never reached inside - can be confirmed or contradicted row by row.
forbidden: TRUSTED does not become proven correct under any outcome of this experiment, and PROVISIONAL does not become probably fine.
A fall in TRUSTED volume is not safer unless the frozen metric and both cost rules say so, and a rise in UNKNOWN or PROVISIONAL is not knowledge unless the primary metric moved with it.
A policy that certifies nothing is not the best policy at certifying; it is the absence of a measurement.
Nothing here settles whether an unsampled violation exists. The instrument reports what its own partition can and cannot support, and the answer key stays outside the instrument.
A reduction on `granular/semantic_step` is not a win for a spatial policy under any reading: that entry exists so that this sentence has to be written.

audit_gate: The corpus audit must pass on the whole corpus and must refuse by name: a control entry that declares a region; an entry in two of the three sets; an entry in none; a `/3` or `/4` file with an empty control list; a `/4` arm that omits its certify criterion or a `/3` arm that states one; a plan that omits either bar; a pilot scope naming an arm, an entry, a budget or a seed the file does not measure; a new entry whose on-paper resolvability claim the instrument contradicts - the expected-share half of that sentence is not a loader rule, because an entry's expectation of a metric is prose in its own record and no field carries it, and it is checked instead by `analysis/e1-5-deciding-entry-prerun.json`; a variable the model has no parameter for; a truth source taken from inside the instrument; two new entries declaring one mechanism.
reproduction_gate: Before any E1.5 arm is read: re-measure all eleven committed E1.x arms, all eight committed E1.3b arms and all four committed E1.4 arms with the binary that will run this experiment, into scratch namespaces, and require every field those documents declare to be identical, with `wall_ms` excluded as non-identity and with only the fields this phase names as additions allowed to appear. A committed field that moved is a defect in the certify axis default and stops the run.
not_claims: that PROVISIONAL means probably safe. It means quiet, at a scale or a density this experiment does not certify at.
that TRUSTED will come to mean proven correct. It means quiet under the channels that ran, stated with the scale and the evidence it was granted at.
that this experiment resolves E1.3, whose condition failed and stays failed, or re-decides E1.4.
that a smaller over-claim number is by itself a safer instrument; the cost rules are what make it readable.
that any of this generalises past the one- and two-dimensional analytically declared models in this corpus.
limitations_this_does_not_remove: Both bars are plan constants, so certified-at-the-right-scale is measured against resolutions this experiment derived and chose, not ones the model declared. A different `certify_share` gives different numbers, and the sensitivity is reported rather than argued away.

Certification depth is bounded by the sample floor and the cap, so every reading is a statement about this budget ladder. Whether the trade survives at 5120 and 10240 evaluations is a different experiment.

The corpus is four new declared regions and two carried entries, all analytically declared, all at one or two parameters. Nothing here speaks to a ten-parameter model, where 2^-8 of a domain is a much finer claim than it is here.

Truth is read only by the metric layer. That makes the primary metric computable without an answer key and also means the instrument cannot tell a quiet coarse cell that is genuinely clean from one that is genuinely violated, which is the limitation this whole experiment is about and no arm here removes.

The deciding entries are box-declared because the union is only exact there, so this experiment says nothing about whether a curved region's over-claim is a scale phenomenon - on a carved entry the decomposition is a lattice estimate and cannot carry a cost rule.
amended_before_running: Five sentences changed on 2026-10-19, after the freeze and before any E1.5 arm ran, in the same direction E1.4's single amendment moved: a factual claim contradicted by the instrument or by the corpus contract is corrected, and no threshold, ceiling, tolerance, criterion or set that decides an outcome is touched. (1) `granular/semantic_step` was listed in `entries.control` and is now in `entries.resolvable`, because the contract on the control set is that its entries declare no region and this one declares a region deliberately. (2) Its description said the fault would be quiet under every channel; the truth layer cannot author that, because a declared region *is* the model's own rule failing and `aporia-properties` gives a fired rule an uncalibrated absolute strength precisely so that a mild violation still flags - measured on the committed corpus, that design is why no box-declared entry certifies its region. The entry's role is unchanged and so is every rule that reads it. (3) `primary_metric.exactness` claimed that no carved entry is in `entries.run`. `granular/tolerance_stack`, carried over from E1.3b as the cost side of the comparison, carves a `where`: its declaration predates this freeze and rewriting a committed entry's truth to fit a new freeze is the one thing the immutability rule forbids. The claim is corrected to state which entries are boxes and which are carved, and to require the analysis to report the deciding figure over all applicable rows and over the box-only subset, rather than dropping the entry from the deciding set - which would have moved a deciding set to keep the story, the exact thing E1.4's amendment refused to do. (4) `granular/quiet_band`'s record carries the design claim that the default instrument certifies at least 0.05 of the region it declares. That claim was measured before any arm of the comparison ran, on the frozen plan's own configuration with the default policy alone - four budgets, five seeds, twenty rows, published as `analysis/e1-5-deciding-entry-prerun.json` with the binary's sha256 and the commit it was built from. It comes out at 0.06875 under the aggregation the primary metric names, so the prediction holds, and the mean is carried by five rows, every one of them at the smallest frozen budget of 320 evaluations: at 640, 1280 and 2560 the instrument certifies nothing inside the band, because by then the sampler has reached it. This is stated here rather than left for the analysis to discover, because it locates the experiment's whole deciding signal - a paired comparison on the central entry is a comparison at 320 evaluations, and an arm that lowers the mean there is a rule that stopped certifying at the smallest scale the plan permits, which the cost rules and the per-budget breakdown are what will tell apart from a gain. No threshold, ceiling, criterion or deciding set moved with this sentence, and the 0.05 stands exactly where this file put it. (5) `audit_gate` named a refusal for a contradicted expected-share claim. The audit implements the resolvability half, where `reach` classes the entry from the partition rule and a claim the arithmetic denies is refused from the set; it cannot implement the other half, and adding a schema field to hold a prediction after the entries were written would have changed the record contract this freeze did not authorise. The gate sentence now says which half the audit refuses and names the artifact that checks the rest.
